Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights: More Than Backup Irons

by Dave Chesson

September 4, 2026

0 comments

3
(3)

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 8:16
Instaread

Tall enough for suppressors and built for low light, Night Fision’s tritium sights also give optic-equipped pistols a dependable iron-sight option.

Suppressor-height sights used to have a pretty specific job. They were tall enough to clear a suppressor and still give you a usable sight picture. Today, they also show up on plenty of optic-equipped pistols as backup irons.

Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights take that traditional tall-sight design and add bright tritium inserts, rugged steel construction, and several sight-color options. I spent time with them to see whether the extra height and bright sight picture actually translate into something useful on the gun.

Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights Specs

  • Material Steel
  • Tritium? Front and rear
  • Sight Picture 3 dot

Night Fision Suppressor Sights Explained

Night Fision builds its Suppressor Height Sights from CNC-machined steel and finishes them with black nitride for added wear and corrosion resistance. The sights use Swiss tritium and Night Fision’s Perfect Dot system, which surrounds the tritium vial with an injection-molded ring intended to remain visible during daylight as well as low light.

The current Glock Suppressor Height line offers fluorescent and phosphorescent front-ring options. Depending on the configuration, front-ring colors include white, orange, yellow, red, blue, and glowing orange or yellow. Rear configurations also vary.

Night Fision currently lists suppressor-height versions for a broad range of Glock pistols, including popular models such as the Glock 17, 19, 26, 34 and 45. Fitment varies by model, so I would check Night Fision’s compatibility information before ordering rather than assuming one sight set fits every Glock.

Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights Features

1 Tall

Suppressor height indicates they are taller than standard iron sights so you can see over a suppressor or co-witness with a red dot sight.

2 Sight Picture

Features a standard 3 dot sight picture with tritium lamps and a bright outlined front sight.

3 Bright Front Sight

Bright front sight draws the eye quickly to the front sight for sight alignment.

 

My Review of Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights 

The standout feature of Night Fision night sights is their unparalleled brightness, especially in low-light scenarios. I recall the stark difference between my previous sights and these luminous tritium-powered vials. The glow emitted in darker settings is nothing short of impressive and provides an invaluable layer of security.

Crafted from high-quality steel and materials akin to bulletproof glass, these sights exude durability. They feel robust, a testament to their resilience, ensuring they can withstand the rigors of frequent use without compromise.

Precision is non-negotiable when it comes to firearm accessories. These Night Fision sights have greatly enhanced my accuracy, particularly when paired with a red dot. The co witness capability maintains clear visibility through the red dot while offering excellent clarity for iron sights when necessary.

I love how they fit seamlessly into various setups. Whether it’s for an optics-ready stealth rig or a co witness selector, these sights just click into place without any fuss.

During daytime shooting, especially with the yellow variants, these sights are not the best. Their real magic lies in low-light conditions, where their tritium-powered glow truly shines, but their performance during the day, especially in well-lit conditions, might not blow you away as much as their nighttime glow.

The dot-over-line and dot-over-dot styles give you choices that suit your shooting style. Plus, the options for rear ring colors and compatibility with different firearm models add that personal touch to your setup.

They don’t just look and feel sturdy; they actually last. I’ve put these sights through some serious shooting sessions, and they’ve held up impressively well without compromising their performance.

They might pack a punch, but they’re not a headache to install. With the right tools and a bit of precision, you can set these sights set up without a hassle. During installation, I followed a process similar to that of Glock sights, requiring precision and specific tools. Utilizing a sight pusher might streamline the installation process, though opting out didn’t significantly impact the overall performance.

The lower third design of these sights struck a balance between providing a clear view through the red dot and maintaining iron sight visibility, a notable advantage during varied shooting conditions.

Let’s be real, these sights aren’t the most budget-friendly. While they’re worth the investment for their performance, they might stretch the wallet a bit for some shooters. Considering their longevity and the security they provide in low-light scenarios, I would say they are a worthy investment but your mileage may vary.

Transitioning from standard sights to these suppressor height ones might take a bit of getting used to, especially for shooters accustomed to different sight profiles.

Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights Pros and Cons 

  • Suppressor Height – If you are running a suppressor, you will need taller sights so you can aim.
  • Bright Front Sight – The bright outline around the front tritium of the front sight attracts your eye.
  • Co-witness – Depending on your optic set up, these may co-witness with your red dot sight.
  • Tall – If you are not using a suppressor, these stick out more and can snag on clothing or gear.

Final Thoughts

Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights do what I want a set of night sights to do. They’re bright when the light disappears; they’re built to survive hard use; and the tall sight picture gives shooters running a suppressor a usable set of irons.

The important distinction today is that suppressor height and optic height aren’t necessarily the same thing. If your primary goal is achieving a specific co-witness with a red dot, Night Fision’s Optics Ready Stealth line gives you more precise height options for that purpose.

If you actually need suppressor clearance and want bright tritium sights to go with it, though, the Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights remain an easy option to recommend. They provide shooters with a dependable option without drastically altering the shooting experience, so I included them in my best night sights for Glocks article.

What You’ll Need for Installation

Real Avid Master Sight Pusher

A quality sight pusher makes removing factory sights and installing the Night Fision rear sight considerably easier while giving you much more control over alignment.

Real Avid 4-in-1 Glock Tool

Handles the front sight screw, along with several other common Glock maintenance jobs.

Real Avid Smart-Fit Vise Block for Glock

Supports the pistol while working on the sights or performing other maintenance, without improvising a work surface.

Threadlocker


A small amount of the appropriate threadlocker can help secure the front sight screw. Follow Night Fision’s installation instructions rather than simply grabbing the strongest threadlocker available.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights work with red dots?
They can, but the resulting co-witness depends on the optic, mounting plate, slide cut and sight height. Night Fision recommends choosing sights based on the complete setup rather than assuming all suppressor-height sights will provide a lower-third co-witness.

What is the difference between Night Fision Suppressor Height and Optics Ready Stealth sights?
Suppressor Height sights are designed primarily to provide sight clearance over a suppressor. Optics Ready Stealth sights are offered in multiple blade heights specifically to achieve different co-witness relationships with pistol optics.

Do Night Fision sights need batteries?
No. Their illumination comes from self-powered tritium inserts, so there are no batteries to replace.

Are Night Fision Suppressor Height Sights available for every Glock?
No. Night Fision lists numerous compatible Glock models, but compatibility varies. Buyers should verify their exact model before ordering.

Can I install Night Fision sights myself?
Yes, if you have the correct tools and experience, but Night Fision officially recommends having a gunsmith install them.
